- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (≥10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope afterward.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or use sentiment as a dampening factor.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and align with sentiment momentum rather than raw history.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–8% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If sentiment is rising steadily, model often underestimates upside; add 2–5% buffer to forecast if sentiment >0.6 over 3+ days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 5–10% gap), reduce forecast by 3–5% for next period unless sentiment is bullish.
